Ascending the Siamese throne in 1782 following the deposition of King Taksin, this monarch became the first ruler of the Chakri dynasty and founded the city that is now Bangkok — who was he?
Rama I: King of Siam from 1782 to 1809.
A Labour politician who served two decades on the Kensington and Chelsea council, she also worked as a senior lecturer at Kingston University — who is she?
Rima Horton: English former councillor and economics lecturer (born 1947)
From 1904 to 1905, two empires clashed over rival ambitions in Manchuria and Korea, fighting major naval battles in the Yellow Sea and the Sea of Japan — which war was this?
Russo-Japanese War: 1904–1905 conflict in East Asia.
Inspired by a 4th-century Greek bishop known for secret gift-giving, this white-bearded, red-suited figure is said to deliver presents by sleigh on Christmas Eve — who is he?

Santa Claus: Legendary Christmas figure. Santa Claus is a legendary figure originating in Western Christian culture who is said to bring gifts during the late evening and overnight hours on Christmas Eve.
Named after the TV show in which its founder played a fictional president, this Ukrainian political party has ruled since Volodymyr Zelenskyy won the presidency in 2019 — which party?
Servant of the People: Political party in Ukraine. It was formed in late 2017 and was officially registered on 31 March 2018 on the basis of the previously registered Party of Decisive Changes.
Ruling from 893 to 927, this monarch's campaigns against the Byzantines and Magyars brought the First Bulgarian Empire to its greatest size and a cultural Golden Age — who was he?
Simeon I of Bulgaria: First Emperor of the Bulgars from 893 to 927.

Before the Civil War he taught at the Virginia Military Institute; historians rank this Confederate general among the most gifted tacticians in U.S. history, and he died in 1863 from wounds in the war's eastern theater — who was he?
Stonewall Jackson: Confederate States Army general (1824–1863)
A former actor turned anti-establishment politician, this Japanese lawmaker founded a party called Reiwa Shinsengumi and once ran for Tokyo governor — who is he?
Taro Yamamoto: Japanese politician and former actor.
Coregent with his stepmother Hatshepsut for 22 years before ruling alone, this pharaoh led between 17 and 20 victorious military campaigns that brought Egypt's empire to its peak — who is he?
Thutmose III: Pharaoh of Egypt from 1479 to 1425 BC.
The second Rashidun caliph and a father-in-law of the prophet Muhammad, he once set out to kill Muhammad with his sword before a spiritual break led him to convert in 616 — who was he?
After her newspaper-publisher husband was assassinated, she took over La Prensa and went on to become Nicaragua's first female president. Who was she?
Violeta Chamorro: President of Nicaragua from 1990 to 1997.
He began his career studying geology in Gansu before rising to become Premier of China from 2003 to 2013 — which retired Communist Party leader?
Wen Jiabao: Premier of China from 2003 to 2013. Born in Tianjin, Wen joined the Chinese Communist Party in 1965.
Born a Lithuanian polytheist and known as Jogaila as Grand Duke, he converted to Catholicism in 1386, married Queen Jadwiga, and became sole ruler of Poland — who was he?
Władysław II Jagiełło: Grand Duke of Lithuania (1377–1434); King of Poland (1386–1434)
This late-Qing statesman raised and organized the Xiang Army to crush the Taiping Rebellion and helped launch the Tongzhi Restoration — who was he?
Zeng Guofan: Chinese politician and military commander (1811–1872)
Who among these was born first?
Omar Khayyam (born 1048) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was born first?
Stephen Hales (born 1677) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
SQL (founded 1974) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four. MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) is a proprietary multi-paradigm programming language and numeric computing environment developed by MathWorks.
Which of these is a physicist?
John Logie Baird is a physicist. In 1928, the Baird Television Development Company achieved the first transatlantic television transmission.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Ingrid Daubechies is a mathematician. Baroness Ingrid Daubechies ( doh-bə-SHEE; French: [dobʃi]; born 17 August 1954) is a Belgian-American physicist and mathematician at Duke University.
What is the atomic number of Darmstadtium?
Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.
What is the atomic number of Gold?
Gold is a chemical element; its chemical symbol is Au (from Latin aurum) and atomic number 79.
In what year was Janet Yellen born?
Janet Yellen: Yellen is the Eugene E. and Catherine M.
In what year was Hippocrates born?
Hippocrates is also widely recognized for his contributions to medical ethics, being credited with the Hippocratic Oath that remains in use today.
In what year was Zakir Naik born?
Zakir Naik: Zakir Abdul Karim Naik (born 18 October 1965) is an Indian Islamic da'i and orator who focuses on comparative religion.
In what year did Guglielmo Marconi die?
Guglielmo Marconi: In 1929, he was ennobled as a marquess (Italian: marchese) by King Victor Emmanuel III, thus becoming the 1st Marchese di Marconi.
In what year did Ibn Khaldun die?
Ibn Khaldun (27 May 1332 – 17 March 1406, 732–808 AH) was an Arab scholar, historian, philosopher, and sociologist.
In what year was Phosphorus discovered?
Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.

Sukhoi Su-57: Komsomolsk-on-Amur Aircraft Production Association. The Sukhoi Su-57 (Russian: Сухой Су-57; NATO reporting name: Felon) is a twin-engine stealth multirole fighter aircraft developed by Sukhoi.
Which country is Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23 from?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23: Soviet Union. It is a third-generation jet fighter, alongside similar Soviet aircraft such as the Su-17 "Fitter".
Who is credited with discovering Pictor?
Pictor: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Pictor is a constellation in the Southern Celestial Hemisphere, located between the star Canopus and the Large Magellanic Cloud.
Who is credited with discovering Proxima Centauri?
Proxima Centauri: Robert T. A. Innes. Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun, located 4.25 light-years (1.3 parsecs) away in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
Who is credited with discovering Stirling's approximation?
Stirling's approximation: Abraham de Moivre. In mathematics, Stirling's approximation (or Stirling's formula) is an asymptotic approximation for factorials.
Who is credited with discovering Yttrium?
Yttrium: Johan Gadolin. Yttrium is a chemical element; it has symbol Y and atomic number 39.

The first woman to officially attend a Dutch university, she became one of the Netherlands' earliest female physicians and, in 1882, opened the world's first birth control clinic — who was this suffrage leader?
Aletta Jacobs (Dutch; 9 February 1854 - 10 August 1929) was a Dutch physician and women's suffrage activist.
This unit of length equals one ten-billionth of a meter, or 100 picometres, and is named after a 19th-century Swedish physicist — what is it?
Angstrom (ONG-) is a unit of length equal to 1010 m; that is, one ten-billionth of a metre, a hundred-millionth of a centimetre, 0.1 nanometre, or 100 picometres.

This type of blood vessel typically carries oxygen-rich blood away from the heart, though the vessels serving the lungs and an unborn baby's placenta carry deoxygenated blood instead — what's it called?
Artery (from Greek (artr)) is a blood vessel in humans and most other animals that takes oxygenated blood away from the heart in the systemic circulation to one or more parts of the body.

This genus of deciduous trees includes 14 species across two subgenera, one found only in East Asia with low, multi-trunked growth, the other spanning Europe, Asia, and eastern North America. What tree genus is this?

Beech (genus Fagus) is a genus of deciduous trees in the family Fagaceae, native to subtropical (accessory forest element) and temperate (as dominant element of mesophytic forests) Eurasia and North America.

Native to eastern North America with resident populations as far north as Newfoundland, this crested songbird in the crow family has a black, U-shaped collar around its neck and a mostly white chest — name it?
Blue jay (Cyanocitta cristata) is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, native to eastern North America.
This condition results from inflamed, fluid-filled sacs that cushion friction points between bones, tendons, and muscles, commonly striking the shoulder, elbow, hip, or knee — what is it?
Bursitis is the inflammation of one or more bursae in the body.
This American Nobel laureate coined the term 'bioorthogonal chemistry' and studies cell-surface sugars called glycans from her professorship at Stanford — who is she?
Carolyn Bertozzi (born October 10, 1966) is an American chemist and Nobel laureate, known for her wide-ranging work spanning both chemistry and biology.
Present naturally in breast milk and added to infant formula, this essential nutrient is also a building block for a neurotransmitter that controls muscle movement — which compound?
Choline is a cation with the chemical formula +.
This legless, non-venomous lizard native to Europe is often mistaken for a snake despite having smooth, non-overlapping scales and semi-fossorial burrowing habits — what is it called?
Common slow worm (Anguis fragilis) is a non-venomous species of legless lizard native to Europe.

Caused by prolonged exposure to glucocorticoids like cortisol, this collection of symptoms includes abdominal weight gain with thin limbs, a rounded red face, and weak, fragile skin that heals poorly — what's it called?
Cushing's syndrome is a collection of signs and symptoms due to prolonged exposure to glucocorticoids such as cortisol.

This is the practice of communication between representatives of states or institutions aimed at influencing international events, serving as the main instrument through which foreign policy goals are pursued. What is this practice called?
Diplomacy is the communication by representatives of state, intergovernmental, or non-governmental institutions intended to influence events in the international system.
Once hunted nearly to extinction for lamp oil, these true seals of the genus Mirounga are named for the male's large trunk-like snout, with males weighing up to 4,000 kilograms — which animal?
Elephant seal are very large, oceangoing true seals in the genus Mirounga.
This ground-nesting songbird of Europe and the Palearctic sings its signature tune while hovering high over farmland and heath, and now also breeds in Australia and Hawaii — what is it?
Eurasian skylark (Alauda arvensis), commonly referred to in Europe as the lark, is a passerine bird in the lark family, Alaudidae.
Part of the dog family yet famous for a pointed snout and a brush-like tail, the 'true' members of this group belong to the genus Vulpes — what creature is it?
Fox are small-to-medium-sized omnivorous mammals belonging to several genera of the family Canidae.
Caught from a tiny waterborne protist and common in travelers and children, it brings fatty, sticky diarrhea and abdominal pain a week or three after exposure — what is this parasitic illness?
Giardiasis is a parasitic disease caused by the protist enteropathogen Giardia duodenalis (also known as G. lamblia).
Named from Ancient Greek words for 'blood' and 'to make,' this biological process produces up to a hundred billion new blood cells per day in a healthy adult — what is it?
Haematopoiesis (from Ancient Greek (hama) 'blood' and (poien) 'to make'; also hematopoiesis in US English, sometimes h(a)emopoiesis) is the formation of blood cellular components.

Discovered in 2013 deep in South Africa's Rising Star Cave system, this archaic human left behind over 1,500 bones from at least 15 individuals, yet a tiny brain keeps its place in our family tree a puzzle — what species is it?

Homo naledi is an extinct species of archaic human discovered in 2013 in the Rising Star Cave system, Gauteng province, South Africa, part of the Cradle of Humankind, dating back to the Middle Pleistocene 335,000-236,000 years ago.
Aided by Soviet intelligence gathered on the American Manhattan Project, this physicist oversaw the first Soviet nuclear weapon test at Semipalatinsk in 1949 — who is he?
Igor Kurchatov was Soviet nuclear physicist (1903–1960).
With brownish-grey fur and a pinkish-red face, this cold-hardy primate is known colloquially by a wintry nickname referencing the snow in its habitat — which species?
Japanese macaque (Macaca fuscata), also known as the snow monkey, is a terrestrial Old World monkey species that is native to Japan.
This Hungarian-American biochemist spent years pushing past skepticism to lay the groundwork for mRNA vaccines, winning a 2023 Nobel alongside Drew Weissman. Who is she?

Katalin Karikó (born 17 January 1955) is a Hungarian and American biochemist who specializes in ribonucleic acid (RNA)-mediated mechanisms, particularly in vitro-transcribed messenger RNA (mRNA) for protein replacement therapy.
Representing the Nemean Lion slain by Heracles as one of his twelve labors, this zodiac constellation sits between Cancer and Virgo — which constellation?
Leo (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac, between Cancer, the Crab, to the west and Virgo, the Maiden, to the east.
This Berkeley professor upended classical logic by proposing 'fuzzy' mathematics — fuzzy sets, fuzzy logic, fuzzy control, and more — who was he?

Lotfi A. Zadeh (4 February 1921 - 6 September 2017) was a mathematician, computer scientist, electrical engineer, artificial intelligence researcher, and professor of computer science at the University of California, Berkeley.
Sharing the 1963 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on nuclear shell structure, this German-American theorist became only the second woman ever to win that prize, after Marie Curie — who was she?
Maria Goeppert Mayer (ne Goppert; June 28, 1906 - February 20, 1972) was a German-American theoretical physicist who shared the 1963 Nobel Prize in Physics with J. Hans D. Jensen.

This American theoretical physicist and science communicator, a professor at the City College of New York, won a 2021 lifetime achievement award named for a famous science-fiction author, honoring his work bridging science and sci-fi. Who is he?
Michio Kaku (born January 24, 1947) is an American theoretical physicist, science communicator, futurologist, and writer of popular science.
One of the four basic animal tissue types, this contractile tissue comes in skeletal, cardiac, and smooth forms and relies on the proteins actin and myosin to generate movement — name the tissue?
Muscle is a specialised soft tissue, one of the four basic types of animal tissues.
This nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug treats acute pain and osteoarthritis by blocking prostaglandin production, though it carries a risk of liver side effects. Name the drug?
Nimesulide is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with pain medication and fever reducing properties.
Named from the Greek word for 'smell,' this hard, brittle, bluish-white transition metal has the highest density of any stable element and is often alloyed for fountain pen nib tips — which element?
Osmium (from Ancient Greek (osm) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.
This species of hickory tree, native to the Mississippi River region of the southern US and northern Mexico, is the official state nut of five states and the state tree of Texas. What nut is this?
Pecan (pih-KAN,; Carya illinoinensis) is a species of hickory native to the Southern United States and northern Mexico in the region of the Mississippi River.
Someone who specializes in matter, motion, and force through space and time earns the title 'physicist' — so what is the field they devote themselves to?
Physics is the scientific study of matter, its fundamental constituents, its motion and behavior through space and time, and the related entities of energy and force.
A strongly alkaline, water-soluble salt of carbonic acid, which compound with the formula K2CO3 is used in glassmaking and Dutch-process chocolate?
Potassium carbonate is the inorganic compound with the formula K2CO3. It is deliquescent, often appearing as a damp or wet solid.
This set of three positive whole numbers, like (3, 4, 5), satisfies a squared plus b squared equals c squared and forms the side lengths of a right triangle — what is it called?
Pythagorean triple consists of three positive integers a, b, and c, such that a2 + b2 = c2.
Beyond his Nobel-winning work in quantum electrodynamics, he explained the superfluidity of supercooled liquid helium and built the parton model — which physicist?
Richard Feynman (May 11, 1918 - February 15, 1988) was an American theoretical physicist.
Nicknamed the seven-year itch, this contagious skin condition is caused by a microscopic burrowing mite and thrives in crowded places like prisons and care homes — what is it?
Scabies (also sometimes known as the seven-year itch) is a contagious human skin infestation by the tiny (0.2-0.45 mm) mite Sarcoptes scabiei, variety hominis.
Element number 14 is a tetravalent non-metal sometimes called a metalloid, prized for the transistors and integrated circuits it makes possible — which one is it?
Silicon is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
The largest order of reptiles, this group is set apart by movable quadrate bones that let snakes gape their jaws around oversized prey — what's the order called?
Squamata (Latin squamatus, 'scaly, having scales') is the largest order of reptiles; most members of which are commonly known as lizards, with the group also including snakes.
This Polish far-right entrepreneur and tax advisor placed third in the 2025 presidential election while chairing a libertarian party and co-leading a far-right coalition — who is he?
Sławomir Mentzen (born 20 November 1986) is a Polish far-right politician, entrepreneur and tax advisor.
Known in medical Latin as the pollex, this digit sits outermost on the hand when you stand palms-forward — which body part?
Thumb is the first digit of the hand, next to the index finger.
The two major groups of these reptiles, side-necked and hidden-necked, differ in how they pull in the head — and they breathe air despite many living in water. What animal?
Turtle (order Testudines) are reptiles characterized by a special shell developed mainly from their ribs, as well as keratinized toothless beak.

Its small molecule packs a surprising punch: strong polarity, relentless hydrogen bonding, and a starring role as the fluid of all known life and the main stuff of Earth's oceans — what compound is it?
Water is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula H2O.

First identified in 1789 and not manufactured at scale until the 1920s, this corrosion-resistant, silvery-grey metal resembles hafnium and takes its name from the mineral that remains its main source — what element, symbol Zr, is it?
Zirconium is a chemical element; it has symbol Zr and atomic number 40.
Produced by oxidizing adrenaline and named for its deep violet color, this compound was studied in the mid-20th century as a possible cause of schizophrenia — what is it?
Adrenochrome: Chemical compound. It was the subject of limited research from the 1950s through to the 1970s as a potential cause of schizophrenia.
This Austrian psychotherapist broke from Freud's circle to found 'individual psychology,' emphasizing birth order and coining the term 'inferiority complex' — who was he?
Named after a French physicist considered a father of electromagnetism, this SI base unit measures electric current and equals one coulomb per second — which unit?
Ampere: SI base unit of electric current. The ampere (symbol: A), often shortened to amp, is the unit of electric current in the International System of Units (SI).
This Soviet single-engine biplane, in production from 1947 to 2001, doubles as a crop-duster, water bomber, and paratroop transport thanks to its rugged, adaptable airframe — what is it?
Antonov An-2: Soviet single-engine civilian aircraft.
Caused by the parasitic roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides and spread through food tainted with eggs, this infection most often hits children and is symptomless in over 85% of cases — what is it?
Ascariasis: Disease caused by the parasitic roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides. The eggs hatch in the intestines, the larvae burrow through the gut wall, and migrate to the lungs via the blood.
Squat-bodied and built for digging, this group includes the European, ferret, honey, and American species despite not truly sharing one family tree — what are they?
Native to Southeast Asia, the heart-shaped leaves of this pepper-family vine are chewed with areca nut, despite links to serious health risks — which plant?
Betel: Species of plant. Betel (Piper betle) is a species of flowering plant in the pepper family Piperaceae, native to Southeast Asia.

Commonly called the Triple Seven, this American wide-body airliner is the world's largest twinjet and the most-built wide-body airplane. It was designed to bridge the gap between the twin-engined 767 and quad-engined 747. What is it?
This Asian insect species, first found in Pennsylvania in 1998, cost Mid-Atlantic apple growers $37 million in a single year and now threatens hazelnut harvests worldwide — what is it?

Brown marmorated stink bug: Species of Pentatomid insect. The brown marmorated stink bug (Halyomorpha halys) is an insect in the family Pentatomidae, native to China, Japan, Korea, and other Asian regions.
Cultivated since China's Song Dynasty and boasting thousands of ornamental cultivars, which flowering shrub from the tea family is native to forests of China and Japan?
Camellia japonica: Species of flowering plant.
Nicknamed the pudding-pipe tree, this Fabaceae-family plant is the national tree of Thailand and doubles as the state flower of Kerala and Delhi — which species?

Cassia fistula: Species of flowering plant. Cassia fistula, also known as golden shower, purging cassia, Indian laburnum, kani konna, or pudding-pipe tree, is a flowering plant in the family Fabaceae.

Convicted in 2013 for leaking nearly 750,000 classified documents to WikiLeaks while serving as an Army intelligence analyst in Iraq, this whistleblower had her sentence commuted by President Obama in 2017 — who is she?
Chelsea Manning: American activist and whistleblower (born 1987)
A political scientist studying voter turnout and race, this scholar rose through Harvard's deanships to become its 30th president in 2023 — only to resign months later; who is she?
Claudine Gay: American political scientist and university administrator (born 1970)
Widespread across Europe, Asia, and Africa, this small predatory falcon has occasionally strayed as far as Guam and the U.S. east coast — what bird is it?
Common kestrel: Species of bird. In the United Kingdom, where no other kestrel species commonly occurs, it is generally just called the "kestrel".

Published in 1750 by a mathematician who described it for any number of unknowns, this linear algebra formula solves systems of equations using determinants of the coefficient matrix — what's it called?
Cramer's rule: Formula for systems of linear equations.
Known as the "grandfather of behavioral economics," this psychologist developed prospect theory with Amos Tversky and won the 2002 Nobel in economics — who was he?
Daniel Kahneman: Israeli-American psychologist and economist (1934–2024)
Named from the Latin word for 'finger' and best known through the common foxglove species, which plant genus produces tall spikes of tubular, often purple flowers?
Digitalis: Genus of flowering plants in the family Plantaginaceae.

Historically nicknamed 'the bloody flux,' this type of gastroenteritis is usually caused by Shigella bacteria or a parasitic amoeba and spreads through contaminated food and water — what is this illness?
Dysentery: Intestinal inflammation causing bloody diarrhea.
Praised by Einstein as the most important woman in the history of mathematics, she proved a theorem linking physical symmetries to conservation laws — who is she?

Comprising more than 700 species mostly native to Australia, these trees and shrubs have oil-gland leaves and a fused 'cap' of sepals and petals covering the stamens, inspiring their Greek-derived name?
This membranous bodily structure comes in superficial, visceral, and deep types, and a dangerous pressure buildup within it can cause compartment syndrome — what is it called?
Fascia: Layer of connective tissue in the body.
Sold under the brand name Prozac, this SSRI treats depression, OCD and panic disorder, and is also prescribed off-label for premature ejaculation — what is it?
Fluoxetine: SSRI antidepressant. It is also approved for treatment of major depressive disorder in adolescents and children 8 years of age and over.
Tucked beneath the liver, this pear-shaped organ stores and concentrates bile before releasing it to aid fat digestion in the small intestine — which organ?
Gallbladder: Organ in humans and other vertebrates.

This Italian friar and cosmological theorist proposed that stars were distant suns with their own planets, and was tried for heresy by the Roman Inquisition for insisting the universe is infinite — who was he?
Giordano Bruno: Italian Dominican friar, philosopher and mathematician (1548–1600)
Unlike its rocky, mountain-dwelling marmot relatives, this solitary lowland rodent — also called the woodchuck — is common across the Eastern U.S., Canada, and Alaska. What is it?
Groundhog: Species of rodent. The groundhog (Marmota monax), also known as the woodchuck, is a rodent of the family Sciuridae, belonging to the group of large ground squirrels known as marmots.

Often defined as the normal functioning of the body free of disease, pain, or injury, this multidimensional state of well-being can be promoted by exercise and sleep and harmed by smoking or stress — what's the one-word concept?
Health: Desirable level of functional or metabolic efficiency of a living being.
Also called urticaria, this skin condition brings red or flesh-colored raised, itchy bumps that may sting and often follow an allergic reaction — what is it?
Hives: Skin disease characterized by red, raised, and itchy bumps.
Defined as a blood level above 5.5 mmol/L, this elevated-potassium condition can trigger a dangerous heart rhythm and even cardiac arrest — what is it called?
Hyperkalemia: Excess potassium in the blood. Normal potassium levels are between 3.5 and 5.0 mmol/L (3.5 and 5.0 mEq/L) with levels above 5.5 mmol/L defined as hyperkalemia.

ISO 56000:2020 defines it as "a new or changed entity, realizing or redistributing value" — but the everyday version is the practical implementation of ideas, the cousin of invention focused on newness, improvement, and the spread of technologies. What's the word?
Innovation: Practical implementation of improvements. Innovation is the practical implementation of ideas that result in the creation or improvements of goods or services.
Mentored by Louis Leakey, this English primatologist spent six decades at Gombe and revealed that chimpanzees use tools and form lasting social bonds — who was she?
Committed to accuracy and verification, this occupation and set of methods involves gathering and distributing the day's news — what field is it?
Journalism: Production of reports on current events.
Named from a Wiradjuri word imitating its own call, this Australian tree kingfisher's cackling laugh is a go-to sound effect for movie jungle scenes — what is it?
Kookaburra: Genus of birds (terrestrial tree kingfishers)
Distinguished by coloured scales, large triangular wings, and a nectar-sipping proboscis, which insect order encompasses both butterflies and moths?
Lepidoptera: Order of insects including moths and butterflies.
Based on the L-188 Electra airliner and distinguished by a tail 'stinger' used to magnetically detect submarines, this four-engine turboprop has served the US Navy since the 1960s — which aircraft?
Lockheed P-3 Orion: Maritime patrol and anti-submarine aircraft family.
Known historically as 'magnesia alba' to distinguish it from a manganese-containing mineral called 'magnesia nigra,' this white hygroscopic solid has the formula MgO — what is it?
Magnesium oxide: Chemical compound naturally occurring as periclase.
Awarded a share of the 1954 Nobel Prize in Physics for his statistical interpretation of the wavefunction, this Göttingen-trained theorist helped found quantum mechanics — who is he?
First isolated in 1921 and encoded by the codon AUG, this essential amino acid also serves as the precursor to cysteine — which amino acid is this?
Most under a millimeter long, these eight-legged arachnids include the parasite that plagues honeybee colonies and the species behind scabies in humans — what are they?
Its Inuktitut name means 'the bearded one,' and males emit a strong odor during rut to attract mates — which thick-coated Arctic mammal is this?
Muskox: Species of arctic land mammal.
Popularized by neurologist George Beard in the 1860s, this diagnosis described fatigue, anxiety, and heart palpitations often blamed on the stresses of modern life — what was the condition called?
This biochemical process lets an organism turn food and water into energy and building blocks, and can go wrong with too much or too little of certain essential substances — what process?
Nutrition: Provision to cells and organisms to support life.
In young children it can mean ear-pulling, extra crying, and poor sleep; it's a group of inflammatory diseases of the middle ear, from acute infections to lingering fluid. What's the medical name?
Otitis media: Inflammation of the middle ear. One of the two main types is acute otitis media (AOM), an infection of rapid onset that usually presents with ear pain.
Cultivated across the tropics for its fragrant essential oil, over 90% of this mint-family herb's global oil supply now comes from Indonesia — which plant?
What is the process by which immune cells like macrophages and neutrophils engulf pathogens and debris with their plasma membrane, forming an internal compartment called a phagosome?
Phagocytosis: Cell membrane engulfing a large particle.
Used in randomized clinical trials as a genuine-looking but pharmacologically inert stand-in — like a sugar pill or saline shot — what's this sham treatment called?
Placebo: Substance or treatment of no therapeutic value.
This rare genetic disorder linked to chromosome 15 leaves affected children constantly hungry, often leading to obesity, alongside a narrow forehead and small hands and feet — what is it?
Prader–Willi syndrome: Genetic disorder involving an imprinted genomic region.
This term covers the laws, regulations, and government actions that address issues from education to healthcare to transportation — what is it?
Public policy: Government proposals, principles and actions.
Found in the Atlas Mountains as the only member of its family native to Africa, this large ruminant's males are called stags and females are hinds — what species is it?
Red deer: Species of hoofed mammal.

This interdisciplinary field combines a power source, mechanical construction, control circuits, and software to design machines that assist humans in fields from medicine to space exploration — what is it?
Robotics: Design, construction, use, and application of robots.
Native to Mexico and Guatemala, this mint-family plant is prized for its hydrophilic seeds known as chia — what's its scientific name?
Salvia hispanica: Species of flowering plant in the mint family.
Located between the bladder and the rectum in male mammals, this paired accessory gland produces most of the fluid released during ejaculation — what is it?
Seminal vesicles: Pair of simple tubular glands.

A parasomnia in which wakefulness and deep non-REM sleep occur in different brain regions at once, this condition can produce anything from bathroom trips to attempts at cooking or even driving — what is it?
Sleepwalking: Sleeping phenomenon combined with wakefulness.

Synthesized by Aristotle and taken as fact for two millennia, this superseded theory held that maggots could arise straight from dead flesh, until Louis Pasteur helped discredit it — what was it called?
Spontaneous generation: Theory of life arising from non-living matter.
Born from Russia's PAK FA programme begun in 1999 and carrying the internal name T-50, this twin-engine jet was the first Russian military aircraft built with stealth technology — what is it?
Sukhoi Su-57: Russian stealth multirole fighter aircraft.
From Greek for 'arrangement' and 'method', this science names and classifies organisms into ranked groups — domain, kingdom, phylum, and on down to species — what is the field?

Taxonomy (biology): Science of classifying organisms. The principal ranks in modern use are domain, kingdom, phylum (division is sometimes used in botany in place of phylum), class, order, family, genus, and species.
